source_text.body:
Run a daily personal agent on a Raspberry Pi
The poster ran OpenClaw for about 13 weeks via Telegram on a Raspberry Pi, handling memory, crons, subagents, research workflows, APIs and scheduled tasks.
·
May 18, 2026
Done with
OC
OpenClaw
What they did
The poster ran OpenClaw on a Raspberry Pi for about 13 weeks as a Telegram-based personal assistant, with memory, cron jobs, subagents, research/summarization workflows, external APIs, reminders, and small automations across files and tools. Their pattern was that the human set direction, the main agent coordinated, subagents handled bounded analysis or coding, and the main agent verified; they also had to redesign brittle flows, like making child agents write results directly when parent readback failed.
How it went
It became daily infrastructure for scheduled checks, recurring analysis, debugging, config reviews, and follow-up, with the main win being continuity across days. It was still rough: model/config failures, update drift, shell quoting bugs, ACP runtime errors, and Pi resource pressure meant regular debugging and cleanup.
Worth knowing
The clearest catch was operational overhead: they archived one dead project after it bloated to about 1.6 GB, and they advise starting with one messaging channel, one model, one cron, and one real workflow.
Try it yourself
with
OpenClaw
Copy prompt
Set up yourself as my daily assistant on my [Raspberry Pi or other always-on machine], reachable through [Telegram]. Keep persistent memory of my preferences, and schedule a daily morning message with [news topics, calendar, and tasks I care about]. Add one research workflow I can trigger by messaging you a topic, and confirm each scheduled task works by running it once. Before sending messages to anyone but me or spending money through any API, show me what you're about to do and wait for my approval.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/openclaw/comments/1ta6cca/roughly_3_month_running_openclaw_as_my_daily
